title: Ulterior Transactions and the Anatomy of a Game
coreMove: Read the social sentence and the psychological invitation as two different messages before you decide whether to play.
sourcePressure: Defines ulterior transactions, then introduces the technical game structure: thesis, antithesis, dynamics, switch, and payoff.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Calling any bad habit or conflict a game instead of requiring a hidden level and predictable payoff.

sourceAnchors.name: ulterior transaction
sourceAnchors.detail: the source defines it as a transaction with a visible social level and a hidden psychological level underneath
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The polite sentence is the social level; the invitation hidden under it is the level that decides whether a game begins.

sourceAnchors.name: thesis and antithesis of a game
sourceAnchors.detail: the source defines a game by its plot and the uncomfortable move that refuses the plot at the hidden level
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The antithesis usually feels rude because it answers the hidden demand instead of obeying the polite script.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human

exampleSpecs.audience: a founder receiving a compliment that quietly tests whether she will chase approval
exampleSpecs.stakes: the next funding meeting may be shaped by a hidden status bid
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Claire thanks the investor for the public praise but asks for the specific risk he wants resolved, refusing the vanity hook.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The espresso foam has gone flat by the time the compliment arrives.

exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer conductor hearing a singer's helpful suggestion carry a rank challenge underneath
exampleSpecs.stakes: the rehearsal can become a weekly status game
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Mathieu answers the hidden demand for special status by restating the audition rule without shaming the singer.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "I only thought the altos might sound better if I stood front row," Erin says.

exampleSpecs.domain: shared flat cleaning rota after a passive note appears
exampleSpecs.audience: a housemate deciding whether to answer the note or the accusation under it
exampleSpecs.stakes: three people may enter a months-long grievance pattern
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Grace takes the note off the fridge and asks for a 10-minute rota reset instead of adding a sharper note below it.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The yellow note curls at one corner on the refrigerator door.

exampleSpecs.domain: museum donor tour after a veiled board remark
exampleSpecs.audience: a curator hearing praise that is really an invitation to owe someone
exampleSpecs.stakes: future exhibit choices can be bent by one accepted hidden bargain
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Jonas later spots the switch: the donor's praise became a claim on exhibit placement, so he drafts a neutral policy response.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Three days later, Jonas rereads the donor's email and sees the hook in the second sentence.

exampleSpecs.audience: a teacher fielding a parent's offer that may become control over team decisions
exampleSpecs.stakes: student access to equipment depends on clean boundaries
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: What makes a generous offer turn into a game before the first cheque clears?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: the teacher accepts the donation only through the school fund and names decision authority before the parent can convert help into leverage.

exampleSpecs.audience: a planner hearing a citizen ask a factual question that keeps returning as a trap
exampleSpecs.stakes: the public meeting can get captured by predictable outrage
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hiroshi marks the thesis, switch, and payoff after the meeting, then prepares an antithesis that answers process rather than outrage next time.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You leave the gymnasium with a stack of comment cards and the same exchange repeating in your ears.

skillTargets: identify when a repeated sequence qualifies as a game
choose an antithesis that answers the hidden level
explain why antithesis feels socially awkward

tryThisNowSpec: Write one polite sentence you recently received. Under it, write the possible hidden invitation in five words or fewer.
